--- title: "[Graph.add_connected_caveman_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a connected caveman graph: a ring of near-cliques. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12397-L12515){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_connected_caveman_graph( num_cliques, clique_size, community_attr="community", type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Connected caveman graph](/assets/graphs/add-connected-caveman-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three connected caveman graphs side by side, each clique in its own color: three triangles, three complete graphs on four nodes, and four of them. In each clique one internal edge is moved to point at the next clique, so the cliques form a ring joined by single plain edges and every node keeps its original degree in total." width="100%"} Starts from `num_cliques` separate cliques of `clique_size` nodes (the caveman graph, see `add_caveman_graph()`) and joins them into a ring by rewiring one edge per clique: in each clique, the edge between its first two nodes is removed and the first node is joined to the last node of the previous clique instead. The edge count is unchanged, and each community is now a clique minus one edge, with one edge to each of its two neighbors on the ring. With cliques of `k` nodes, most nodes keep degree `k - 1`; in each clique the second node drops to `k - 2` and the last node rises to `k`. This is Watts's construction, and it matches NetworkX's `connected_caveman_graph()`. Each node's clique (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute. The cliques are created in ring order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In a directed graph every edge inside a clique points from the earlier-created node to the later one, and each ring edge points from a clique's first node back to the previous clique (so the first clique's ring edge points to the last clique). The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Connected caveman graphs are useful for: - test cases for community detection with clear but not perfectly isolated groups - modeling small, tightly knit groups that each have a single tie to the next group - the starting point of Watts's small-world experiments, where random rewiring gradually shortens the paths around the ring ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [num_cliques]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of cliques on the ring. Must be at least `2`. [clique_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each clique. Must be at least `3`, so that each clique still hangs together after losing an edge. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's clique index. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `num_cliques=` is less than `2` or `clique_size=` is less than `3`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four caves of five nodes keep all `4 * 10 = 40` edges, but now form a single connected ring: ::: {#fa5e0b6b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_connected_caveman_graph(num_cliques=4, clique_size=5) graph.count_edges(), graph.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (40, True) ``` ::: ::: The rewiring moves one edge end in each cave, so degrees range from `3` to `5`: ::: {#eea76190 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df()["degree"].value_counts().sort("degree") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
